messages.subject: feedback on data viewer
parts:
Dear Ian
This week I've given Deducer another try, and I must admit that it has
become more stable and usable since the last time. Kudos!

Nevertheless, I would have some comments regarding minor issues and
design decisions that could influence usability, as well as several
requests. In no particular order:
- move 'data.frame' and 'dim' information outside the combobox list,
since it can become practically useless. Here, using a workspace I'm
currently working on, I need to maximize the Data viewer window just
to see in full 'data.frame', and I still cannot see the dimensions
(see 1st screen shot). Moreover, the current arrangement makes the
combo list hard to read. There would be two possible solutions. Add a
status area to the right of the combo that would indicate the info
and/or put this info in a toolitp.

- rm the top-right 'Clear' button since it can be confusing. I'm
always hesitating whether to click the 'Clear' button (a cross) or the
WM cross to close the Data viewer. Am mistake from such confusion
could be costly. Perhaps move it to the left-hand side next to Save?

- to improve consistency and possibly make things more intuitive,
shouldn't 'Edit > Remove data' be called 'Clear data' or 'Remove data
frame'? Shouldn't the top-right button use the same label in the
tooltip?

- implement a "true" 'data view' mode, as opposed to data edit
(currently the 'Data viewer' is more of a 'Data editor' :)). Perhaps
in the form of a read-only switch/button, in which the user cannot
re-order the df columns nor modify arbitrary cells, remove rows/cols,
etc. This would be designed to avoid bugs or unintended modifications.

- put 'Data' item in the Data viewer Menu, too. I believe it's more
intuitive to also have it there, and not only in JGR. Moreover, when
using data.viewer from a non-JGR session, this would allow non-JGR
users to access the data manipulation functionality.

- have a 'filter' view mode (not a data-modifying subset). One of the
features I mostly miss from a spreadsheet and am obliged to work
around using subsetting functions is Filter. It would be great if Data
viewer would allow the user to pick from a combo, for a given variable
(especially factor or character), one of the available values and
dynamically 'subset' the data in read-only mode. This can be very
useful when one needs to check subsets of the data, such as when
synchronising two data sets

- have a 'sort' view mode (not a data-modifying sort operation). A bit
similar to the above, allow the user to sort the data frame in ro
mode.

- select multiple rows/cols (similar to tcltk2::tk2edit() ). Currently
Data viewer allows only to select multiple individual cells. It would
be great if this could be extended to rows/cols, while
moving/re-ordering columns were made a context-menu item.

- select entire row is visually jerky. When you click on a rowname to
select the row, Deducer will first move the screen to the right edge
of the data set and immediately back. It doesn't behave this way when
selecting a column. It's a minor issue, but can be disturbing.

- console monopolization. When running data.viewer() in rterm it will
freeze all of R, disallowing issuing any R command while the Viewer is
visible. Could this be changed?

- a long-time minor request: let the user set the size of the NA font.
In my eyes,

Two more issues more related to Deducer/JGR:
- the size of initial windows can spill outside the available screen.
For example, the script editor window always opens with height 53
lines, when my screen allows a maximum of 47 lines (2nd screenshot).
The Data viewer always opens a window as seen in the 3rd screenshot
(please let me know if I should refrain from sending attachments so
big). In my case, my window manager allows me to quickly maximize the
window vertically or move it using <alt>+mouse until I can find the
bottom/upper handle and resize the window, but this might not
necessarily be the case of other users.

- buttons labels: currently I'm regularly getting truncated button
labels, such as 'Cont...' (continue), 'Ca...' (cancel), '...' ('[1]'
in Data merge), 'Rem...' (remove) and similar. Just try to resize the
window horizontally and you will notice labels truncating. Is it
possible to specify to Java a minimum length for the buttons?

Please let me know what you think of all this. Regards
Liviu

--

messages.subject: Re: feedback on data viewer
parts:
Liviu,

Thank you for your comments. As always they are thoughtful and correct.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
First lets start with the good news:

> - move 'data.frame' and 'dim' information outside the combobox list,
> since it can become practically useless. Here, using a workspace I'm
> currently working on, I need to maximize the Data viewer window just
> to see in full 'data.frame', and I still cannot see the dimensions
> (see 1st screen shot). Moreover, the current arrangement makes the
> combo list hard to read. There would be two possible solutions. Add a
> status area to the right of the combo that would indicate the info
> and/or put this info in a toolitp.
Fixed on rforge. now just the data.frame name is displayed.

> - the size of initial windows can spill outside the available screen.
> For example, the script editor window always opens with height 53
> lines, when my screen allows a maximum of 47 lines (2nd screenshot).
> The Data viewer always opens a window as seen in the 3rd screenshot
> (please let me know if I should refrain from sending attachments so
> big). In my case, my window manager allows me to quickly maximize the
> window vertically or move it using <alt>+mouse until I can find the
> bottom/upper handle and resize the window, but this might not
> necessarily be the case of other users.

My god your screen is small. Are you using your cell phone as a
monitor? :) Fixed on rforge.

> - to improve consistency and possibly make things more intuitive,
> shouldn't 'Edit > Remove data' be called 'Clear data' or 'Remove data
> frame'? Shouldn't the top-right button use the same label in the
> tooltip?

Both now read "Remove data from workspace"

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The above changes are those which I could make in a short amount of
time. The others would require much more thought/effort. I don't see
myself getting to them anytime in the near future (or to be honest the
distant future). I would heartily support you if you wanted to dive in
and work on the problem yourself. hint, hint.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I do have a couple comments on your other comments:

> - select entire row is visually jerky. When you click on a rowname to
> select the row, Deducer will first move the screen to the right edge
> of the data set and immediately back. It doesn't behave this way when
> selecting a column. It's a minor issue, but can be disturbing.

I know. I've known about this since the first version was made.
Interestingly this is a programming problem that I have been unable to
solve.

> - console monopolization. When running data.viewer() in rterm it will
> freeze all of R, disallowing issuing any R command while the Viewer is
> visible. Could this be changed?

no, this can not be changed. The console must be blocked or REALLY bad
things happen due to R being single threaded.

> - buttons labels: currently I'm regularly getting truncated button
> labels, such as 'Cont...' (continue), 'Ca...' (cancel), '...' ('[1]'
> in Data merge), 'Rem...' (remove) and similar. Just try to resize the
> window horizontally and you will notice labels truncating. Is it
> possible to specify to Java a minimum length for the buttons?

It is. But each platform may require a different length depending it's
font. I test on windows and mac.

> - rm the top-right 'Clear' button since it can be confusing. I'm
> always hesitating whether to click the 'Clear' button (a cross) or the
> WM cross to close the Data viewer. Am mistake from such confusion
> could be costly. Perhaps move it to the left-hand side next to Save?

Hopefully the new tooltip will mitigate this on operating systems with
an 'x' in the top right. The mistake is not that costly as a confirm
dialog pops up.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cheers,
Ian
